  The patch introduces duplicate narration controls and multiple document-sized or unbounded hot paths that become problematic for long manuscripts and large provider catalogs. Focused tests, typechecking, and the client build pass, but they do not exercise these runtime scaling and composition issues.

Full review comments:

- [P2] Reuse one narration transport instead of mounting another — /home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/root.tsx:80-80
  When narration starts from the editor, analysis page, or personas panel, the existing `SpeechTransport` remains active while this root-level player exposes the same play/pause/skip/seek/stop controls. This creates two synchronized transports for the same session and a fixed overlay that can obscure content on smaller screens; make the local transport trigger-only or compose/suppress it when the global player is present.

- [P2] Cancel superseded grammar passes inside the block loop — /home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/components/editor/grammar-panel.tsx:79-80
  With the grammar desk open on a long draft, every edit schedules another full scan, but the generation token is checked only after every paragraph has been linted. If a pass takes longer than the debounce interval, obsolete passes continue issuing one worker request per block even after another edit or panel close, causing CPU backlog and delayed suggestions; check cancellation inside the loop or batch/incrementally lint the document.

- [P2] Stop walking the manuscript DOM on every audio tick — /home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/components/ui/global-speech-player.tsx:311-311
  During manuscript narration, `audio.ontimeupdate` dispatches `twyne:speech` several times per second, and each event evaluates `root.textContent`, traversing the entire editor DOM before updating the highlight. This produces continuous document-sized main-thread work for long drafts; track mutations with a `MutationObserver` or dirty/version flag instead of rescanning on every playback tick.

- [P2] Avoid eagerly mounting controls for every catalog model — /home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/routes/settings/index.tsx:2274-2275
  For providers with large reasoning catalogs, this eagerly renders a complete control for every model and reasoning option, although `reasoningModelsFor` documents that the dial should apply only to the provider's default model. Each rendered `SiteSelect` also installs its own document-level pointer listener, so advanced settings can hydrate an unbounded form and make every pointer event fan out across all controls; restrict this to the active/default model or add progressive disclosure.
